mainTopic: Limits on fasts for rain, praying for rain out of season, and the community's signs of distress when rain does not come
overview: The גמרא tells how רבי יהודה נשיאה declared thirteen fasts (according to רש״י, for a calamity other than rain) with no answer, and רבי אמי stopped him from adding more so the ציבור would not be overburdened. רבי יוחנן and a ברייתא teach that the thirteen-fast limit is only for rain, while for other disasters people keep fasting until they are answered. רבי אמי is defended as following רבי, who argues with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the reason for the limit. The people of נינוה, who need rain even in summer, are told by רבי to ask for it in שומע תפלה like individuals, and the הלכה follows this. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rules for the strict fasts: how far stores may open on Monday and Thursday, that only joyful building and planting are cut back, and that חברים stop greeting each other and sit like mourners. Finally, רבי אלעזר teaches that an important person may fall on his face or wear sackcloth only if he will be answered. He also teaches that different people plead and show honor in different ways, and this last teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Thirteen fasts with no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה declared thirteen fasts (according to רש״י, for a calamity other than rain), was not answered, and thought about declaring more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He declared thirteen fasts and was not answered. He thought about declaring more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: a leader made the community fast thirteen times over a calamity (according to רש״י, not a lack of rain), nothing happened, and he wanted to add more fasts. This sets up the question of whether more fasts are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full set of fasts for rain in the משנה adds up to thirteen. This leader was ready to go past that limit because they still had not been answered. According to רש״י these fasts were for a calamity other than rain, which is why the next steps say the limit should not have applied. The next step tells us whether that was allowed.

phrases.english: He decreed thirteen fasts
phrases.notes: The 'he' is רבי יהודה נשיאה, who is named in the lines just before this.

phrases.english: and he was not answered.
He considered decreeing more.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: after thirteen unanswered fasts, the leader considered adding more.

steps.title: רבי אמי objects to adding more fasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי tells him not to add fasts, because we do not burden the ציבור too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: They already said, we do not trouble the community more than is fitting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes back on the plan to add fasts. He gives a reason: the community should not be overburdened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי's reason is about the people: too many fasts is too heavy a load. Keep this reason in mind, because the rest of the סוגיא asks whether that really is the reason behind the thirteen-fast limit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ אֵין מַטְרִיחִין אֶת הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: Look, they said: We do not trouble the community
excessively.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the plan in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to declare more than thirteen fasts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a rule against overburdening the community, and more than thirteen fasts would break it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No more than thirteen fasts, because the community may not be burdened too much.

steps.title: רבי אמי was ruling on his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says רבי אמי's ruling was his own personal view, not the accepted teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא said: What רבי אמי did, he did on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: A later חכם pushes aside רבי אמי's ruling. He says it was רבי אמי's own opinion, not the main teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא does not say that רבי אמי invented something false. He says that רבי אמי's ruling does not match what the main teaching says. The next step brings that main teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
What Rabbi Ami did —
he did it on his own.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אמי followed his own view, and most חכמים did not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי דַּעֲבַד לְגַרְמֵיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's objection from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אמי's ruling as a binding rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It was his own view, not the accepted teaching.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The limit is only for rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the thirteen-fast limit applies only to rain. For other disasters the community keeps fasting until answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this for rain. But for other kinds of disasters, people keep fasting until Heaven answers them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא now gives the real teaching. The limit on fasts applies only to fasts for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason for the limit were 'don't burden the community,' it would apply to every kind of fast. Since it applies only to rain, the reason must be something specific to rain. So רבי יוחנן's teaching works against רבי אמי's reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: fasts for other disasters have no fixed number. People keep fasting until they are answered.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rather, this is what Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They taught this only for rain,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule that the fasts stop after thirteen.

phrases.english: but for other kinds of calamities —
they keep on fasting
until they are answered from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct teaching that replaces רבי אמי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirteen-fast limit is only for rain. For other disasters, the community fasts until answered.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing: the sets of three and seven fasts were said only about rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: When they said three and when they said seven, they meant only for rain. But for other disasters, people keep fasting until they are answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said. This backs up his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'three' and 'seven' are the sets of fasts in the משנה. Together with the first three fasts, they add up to thirteen. The ברייתא limits all of these to rain, just like רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
When they said three and when they said seven —
they said it only for rain,
but for other kinds of calamities —
they keep on fasting until they are answered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that the limit applies only to rain
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: Does this disprove רבי אמי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא is a full refutation of רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי אמי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא knocks down רבי אמי's view. It is setting up an answer in his defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said the reason for the limit is not to burden the community. If that were true, the limit would apply to all fasts. The ברייתא limits it to rain only, so it seems to prove רבי אמי's reason wrong.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rabbi Ami!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא of step 5 against רבי אמי's view from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's reason (not burdening the community)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If burden were the reason, it would apply to every fast. The ברייתא limits it to rain only.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי can say that תנאים argue about the reason. רבי holds it is about burdening the community, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the rainy season has ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי could answer you: This is a מחלוקת of תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: We do not decree more than thirteen fasts on the community, because we do not burden the community too much. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: That is not the reason. It is because the time of the rainy season has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אמי. It shows that a תנא (רבי) gave the same reason he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reasons for the thirteen-fast limit. רבי says the reason is not to burden the community, and that is רבי אמי's view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the reason is that by then the rainy season is over, and the ברייתא in step 5 fits his view. So רבי אמי is not refuted; he simply follows רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute among תנאים
this is not for that reason

steps.whatToRemember: The thirteen-fast limit has two possible reasons. רבי and רבי אמי say it is so we do not burden the community. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is because the rainy season is over, which is why it applies only to rain.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that there are only thirteen fasts for rain. They argue only about WHY, and that 'why' decides whether the limit also covers other disasters.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami could say to you:
It is a dispute of tanna'im, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר,
phrases.english: We do not decree more than thirteen fasts on the community,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַטְרִיחִין אֶת הַצִּבּוּר יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי,
phrases.english: because we do not trouble the community excessively,
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
This is not for that reason,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּצָא זְמַנָּהּ שֶׁל רְבִיעָה.
phrases.english: but because the time of the rainfall has passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי אַמֵּי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the question is a dispute among תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to disprove רבי אמי's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי follows רבי. The ברייתא of step 5 follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The people of נינוה ask about summer rain
steps.stepSummary: The people of נינוה, who need rain even in the summer, ask רבי whether they pray for it as individuals or as a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of נינוה sent to רבי: People like us, who need rain even in the season of תמוז, what should we do? Are we like individuals or like a community? Are we like individuals, and so we ask in 'שומע תפלה'? Or are we like a community, and so we ask in ברכת השנים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. A city with an unusual climate asks where in the שמונה עשרה it should ask for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A community's request for rain goes in ברכת השנים. An individual's personal request goes in שומע תפלה. The question is whether a whole city counts as a 'community' when its need is different from the rest of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessing for the year's crops

phrases.english: The people of Nineveh sent to Rabbi:
Such as us, who even in the season of Tammuz
need rain, what should we do?
Are we like individuals or are we like a community?
Are we like individuals, and so we ask in 'Who hears prayer',
or are we like a community, and so we ask in the blessing of the years?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a city that needs rain in the summer asks for it as individuals (in שומע תפלה) or as a community (in ברכת השנים).

steps.title: רבי answers: You are like individuals
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that they are like individuals and should ask for rain in שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: You are like individuals, and you ask in 'שומע תפלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the question. Even a whole city counts as individuals here, so they ask for rain in שומע תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though נינוה is a big city, its summer need for rain does not move the request into ברכת השנים. The request stays a private one inside שומע תפלה.
steps.whatToRemember: A place that needs rain at an unusual time, even a whole city, asks for it in שומע תפלה like individuals, not in ברכת השנים.

phrases.english: He sent to them: You are like individuals
and you ask in 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are like individuals and ask for rain in שומע תפלה.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה seems to contradict רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's ruling with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says that nowadays rain requests follow the local years, places and times.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי יהודה said: When do these rules apply? When the years are normal and ישראל lives on its own land. But nowadays, everything follows the years, the places and the time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבי's answer to the people of נינוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the people of נינוה are like individuals and ask for rain only in שומע תפלה. רבי יהודה says the fixed rain schedule was meant for ישראל living in its land. Nowadays each place follows its own climate, so a place that needs rain in summer would ask for it in the regular rain blessing, just as everyone does in the rainy season.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Yehuda said:
When?
phrases.notes: He means: when does the fixed schedule for asking for rain apply?

phrases.english: At a time when the years are as they should be
and Israel is living on its land.
But nowadays,
everything follows the years,
phrases.notes: "Years" here means the local climate and weather.

phrases.english: everything follows the places,
everything follows the time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's answer from step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the people of נינוה ask for rain in שומע תפלה like individuals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה says that nowadays each place asks for rain according to its own climate, which suggests נינוה would ask in the regular rain blessing and not only in שומע תפלה.

steps.title: רבי is a תנא and may disagree
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a ברייתא cannot refute רבי, because רבי is himself a תנא and is allowed to argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are throwing a ברייתא at רבי?! רבי is a תנא, and he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי by pointing out that he has the same rank as רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא only shows the view of one תנא. Since רבי is also a תנא, he is free to argue with רבי יהודה, so there is no real contradiction. It is simply a disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא (here, an outside teaching of the תנאים)
He is a תנא and may disagree

phrases.english: He said to him:
You raise a ברייתא against Rabbi?!
Rabbi is a Tanna, and he disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rank of authority: a תנא may disagree with a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה shows that רבי's ruling is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי and רבי יהודה simply disagree; a ברייתא does not refute a fellow תנא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא, who answered נינוה) is a different person from רבי יהודה, who is quoted in the ברייתא.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since two תנאים argue, the גמרא asks what the law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion on this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical law. This sets up the next step, where אמוראים give their answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10 and 11 left us with a dispute between רבי and רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא wants to know which view we follow when a place needs rain out of season.

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the law after the dispute in steps 10 and 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which blessing does a place that needs rain out of season ask for it?

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says to ask in ברכת השנים, and רב ששת says to ask in שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In ברכת השנים. רב ששת said: In שומע תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן follows רבי יהודה: the request goes in the regular blessing for rain and crops. רב ששת follows רבי: it goes only in שומע תפלה, where any individual may add personal requests.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing for the year's crops and rain (בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ)
The blessing 'Who hears prayer', where personal requests may be added

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: In the blessing of the years.
Rav Sheshet said: In 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with two views
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: ברכת השנים (like רבי יהודה). רב ששת: שומע תפלה (like רבי).

steps.title: The law follows שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב ששת: an out-of-season request for rain goes in שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the law is: in שומע תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on this topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows רב ששת, and through him רבי. A place that needs rain when it is not the rainy season in ארץ ישראל asks for it like an individual, in שומע תפלה.
steps.whatToRemember: When rain is needed outside the normal season, it is requested in שומע תפלה and not in ברכת השנים, following רבי and רב ששת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical practice that communities needing rain out of season add their request in שומע תפלה.

phrases.english: And the law is: in 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views of step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Rain needed out of season is requested in שומע תפלה.

steps.title: The משנה about opening stores on Monday and Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on Monday stores are opened a little at nightfall, and on Thursday all day, because of כבוד השבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday they open the door a little at nightfall, and on Thursday all day, because of the honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes a line from the משנה. This sets up a question about how to read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the strict fasts, business is cut back and stores stay mostly closed. The משנה gives an allowance: on Monday a little opening at dark, and on Thursday more, so people can prepare for שבת. What exactly 'all day' on Thursday means is asked in step 16 and answered in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: They tilt (open the door partly, only a little)

phrases.english: On Monday they open slightly at nightfall
phrases.notes: "Monday" is literally "the second day." מטין means tilting the door, so it is open only a crack.

phrases.english: and on Thursday all day
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns to the משנה's list of fast-day restrictions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Monday the store may be opened slightly at nightfall; on Thursday all day, for כבוד השבת.

steps.title: How should the משנה be read?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether Thursday means a slight opening all day, or a full opening all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: How is it taught? On Monday they open slightly at nightfall, and on Thursday slightly all day, because of כבוד השבת? Or perhaps: on Monday they open slightly, and on Thursday they open fully the whole day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents two possible ways to read the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: the opening is always only slight. Monday allows it at nightfall, and Thursday allows it all day. Reading two: Monday allows a slight opening, and Thursday allows the store to be fully open the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
How is it taught? (how to read the words)

phrases.english: A question was asked of them: How is it taught?
On Monday they open slightly at nightfall,
and on Thursday all day,
phrases.notes: In this first reading, Thursday is still only a slight opening, but it is allowed all day.

phrases.english: because of the honor of Shabbat,
or perhaps: on Monday they open slightly,
and on Thursday they open fully the entire day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the משנה quoted in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does Thursday mean a slight opening all day, or a full opening all day?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that on Thursday the store is fully open
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on Monday they open slightly until evening, and on Thursday they open fully all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it is taught: On Monday they open slightly until evening, and on Thursday they open fully the whole day, because of כבוד השבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word פותחין, meaning a full opening, for Thursday. That supports the second reading. Monday is a slight opening, and Thursday is a full opening for the whole day.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
On Monday they open slightly until the evening,
and on Thursday they open fully the entire day
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second reading: on Thursday the store is opened fully, the whole day.

steps.title: Two doorways, and a platform blocking the door
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: with two doorways, open one and lock one; if a platform hides the door, open normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had two doorways, he opens one and locks one. If he had a platform in front of his doorway, he opens as usual and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds practical details about how a store owner keeps the restriction on these fast days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is that the store should not look open in the normal way. A store with two doorways shows this by using only one. If a platform already blocks the view of the door, nobody sees it open, so there is nothing to worry about.

keyTerms.meaning: A platform or bench (here, blocking the view of the door)

steps.whatToRemember: On the strict fast days, Monday allows only a slight opening of the store, and Thursday allows a full opening for כבוד השבת. What matters is how the store looks from outside.

phrases.english: If he had two doorways,
he opens one and locks one.
If he had a platform opposite his doorway,
he opens in his usual way and need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with practical cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two doorways, open only one; if a platform blocks the doorway, the store may be opened normally.

steps.title: The משנה: If the fasts end with no answer, cut back on business, building and planting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if all these fasts passed and there was still no rain, people reduce business, building and planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If these fasts passed and they were not answered, they reduce business dealings, building and planting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה so it can explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה moves to a new stage. The fasts are over and there is still no rain, so the community now limits everyday activities as a sign of distress.

phrases.english: If these fasts passed and they were not answered —
they reduce business dealings,
building and planting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the משנה's rule about opening stores to its next rule, about what is done after the fasts are finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the fasts end with no rain, people reduce business, building and planting.

steps.title: Only joyful building and planting are reduced
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the building and planting mentioned in the משנה means only building and planting done for joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: building means joyful building. Planting means joyful planting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that narrows the משנה's words: not every kind of building and planting is limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of the משנה could sound like all building and planting must be reduced. The ברייתא limits this to building and planting done for celebration, not for basic needs.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as stopping all building and planting. Only building and planting done for joy are reduced.

phrases.english: It was taught: building — means joyful building.
Planting — means joyful planting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and narrows the words בנין and נטיעה from the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reduction applies only to joyful building and joyful planting.

steps.title: Examples: a wedding house and a royal garden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives examples: joyful building is building a wedding house for one's son, and joyful planting is planting a fancy royal-style garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is joyful building? One who builds a wedding house for his son. What is joyful planting? One who plants a royal garden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues by giving a clear example of each kind of joyful activity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples are things done for celebration or luxury, not for basic living. A wedding house is for a celebration, and a royal-style garden is only for beauty.

keyTerms.meaning: A wedding house built for a son's marriage
A fancy garden like the ones kings plant

phrases.english: What is joyful building? —
This is one who builds a wedding house for his son.

phrases.aramaic: אִי זוֹ הִיא נְטִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה —
phrases.english: What is joyful planting? —
This is one who plants a royal garden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of the joyful building and planting defined in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joyful building is a wedding house for one's son; joyful planting is a royal-style ornamental garden.
steps.whatToRemember: After the fasts, only joyful building and planting are cut back, like a wedding house or a fancy garden.

steps.title: The משנה: Greetings are also reduced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: people also cut back on greeting one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in greetings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה's list so it can explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list of things that are reduced, from step 19. Besides business, building and planting, people also reduce greeting each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Greeting someone, literally asking about his welfare

phrases.english: And in greetings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's list to take up its next item, greetings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greetings are reduced once the fasts end with no rain.

steps.title: How greetings are limited, and sitting like mourners
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חברים do not greet each other at all. If עמי הארץ greet them, they answer quietly and seriously, and they sit wrapped up like mourners until Heaven has mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: חברים do not greet each other at all. When unlearned people greet them, they answer quietly and seriously. They wrap themselves and sit like mourners and like people under a ban, like people rebuked by God, until Heaven has mercy on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains exactly how greetings are reduced, and describes the mood of distress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among חברים, greetings stop completely. Since עמי הארץ may not know this, the חברים answer them, but in a low, serious way. The ברייתא adds that they sit like mourners until the rain comes.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are very careful in keeping מצוות

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
חברים do not greet each other at all.
Unlearned people who do greet them —
they answer them in a weak, quiet voice,
and seriously.
And they wrap themselves and sit
like mourners and like people under a ban,
like people who have been rebuked by God,
until Heaven has mercy on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲבֵרִים, אֵין שְׁאֵילַת שָׁלוֹם בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the reduction of greetings from step 22 works in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חברים stop greeting each other; they answer עמי הארץ quietly and sit like mourners until Heaven has mercy.
steps.whatToRemember: Greetings stop among חברים, but they still answer an unlearned person, quietly and seriously.

steps.title: An important person may not fall on his face unless he will be answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that an important person should not fall on his face in prayer unless he will be answered like יהושע בן נון, proven from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: An important person is not allowed to fall on his face unless he will be answered like יהושע בן נון, as it says: "And ה׳ said to יהושע: Get up, why are you falling on your face?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר about public acts of distress in prayer. It limits when an important person may fall on his face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling on one's face is a strong public act of pleading. רבי אלעזר says an important person should do it only if he will be answered, as יהושע was, because ה׳ answered him right away. The פסוק shows that יהושע fell on his face and ה׳ answered him.

keyTerms.meaning: To fall on his face in prayer

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
An important person is not allowed
to fall on his face,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נַעֲנֶה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
phrases.english: unless he will be answered like Yehoshua bin Nun,
as it says:
"And ה׳ said to Yehoshua:

phrases.aramaic: קֻם לָךְ לָמָּה זֶּה אַתָּה נֹפֵל עַל פָּנֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: Get up, why are you falling on your face?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לִיפּוֹל עַל פָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא about the community's behavior to a new teaching about an important person's public acts of distress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An important person may fall on his face only if he will be answered, like יהושע בן נון.

steps.title: An important person may not wear sackcloth unless he will be answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds that an important person should not put on sackcloth unless he will be answered like יהורם בן אחאב, proven from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: An important person is not allowed to put on sackcloth unless he will be answered like יהורם בן אחאב, as it says: "And when the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes, and he was walking on the wall, and the people saw, and there was sackcloth on his skin..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רבי אלעזר with the same pattern, this time about wearing sackcloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the previous teaching, with a different act of distress. Wearing sackcloth is a public sign of mourning and pleading, so an important person should do it only if he will be answered. The פסוק shows יהורם wearing sackcloth during the crisis.

keyTerms.meaning: To put on sackcloth, a rough garment worn in mourning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לַחֲגוֹר שַׂק
phrases.english: An important person is not allowed to put on sackcloth

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נַעֲנֶה כִּיהוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב,
phrases.english: unless he will be answered like Yehoram son of Achav,
as it says: "And when the king heard

phrases.aramaic: אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָאִשָּׁה וַיִּקְרַע אֶת בְּגָדָיו
phrases.english: the words of the woman, he tore his clothes,
and he was walking on the wall,
and the people saw, and there was the sackcloth
on his skin, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לַחֲגוֹר שַׂק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רבי אלעזר, built just like the first one, applied to sackcloth instead of falling on one's face.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An important person may put on sackcloth only if he will be answered, like יהורם בן אחאב.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר limits two public acts of distress for an important person, falling on his face and wearing sackcloth, to someone who will be answered.

steps.title: משה and אהרן fell on their faces, יהושע and כלב tore their clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that different people plead with ה׳ in different ways. משה and אהרן fell on their faces, while יהושע and כלב tore their clothes. Both points are proven from פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Not everyone pleads by tearing clothes, and not everyone pleads by falling on the face. משה and אהרן fell on their faces, and יהושע and כלב tore their clothes. We know משה and אהרן fell, because the פסוק says, "And משה and אהרן fell on their faces." We know יהושע and כלב tore their clothes, because the next פסוק says, "And יהושע son of נון and כלב son of יפנה tore their clothes."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives another teaching. It matches the idea of the last two steps: how a person pleads with ה׳ depends on his level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling on the face is treated as the higher form, used by the greatest people, משה and אהרן. Their students, יהושע and כלב, used the lesser form of tearing their clothes. The proof comes from two פסוקים next to each other in the story of the spies, where each pair is described doing something different.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's clothes, a sign of grief and pleading
Falling on the face in prayer

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Not everyone [pleads] by tearing [clothes],
and not everyone by falling [on the face].
Moshe and Aharon by falling,
Yehoshua and Kalev by tearing.
Moshe and Aharon by falling,
as it is written: "And Moshe and Aharon fell on their faces."
Yehoshua and Kalev by tearing,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וְכָלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה
phrases.english: as it is written: "And Yehoshua son of Nun and Kalev son of Yefuneh
tore their clothes."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הַכֹּל בִּקְרִיעָה וְלֹא הַכֹּל בִּנְפִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי אלעזר about who may use which form of pleading. It follows his teachings about falling on the face and wearing sackcloth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Falling on the face suited משה and אהרן. Tearing clothes suited יהושע and כלב.

steps.title: The word "and" shows יהושע and כלב did both
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני) challenges רבי אלעזר's reading. The פסוק says "AND יהושע", and that extra "and" may mean יהושע and כלב also fell on their faces, on top of tearing their clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged this, and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני: If the פסוק had said only "יהושע", it would be as you say. But since it says "And יהושע", it means he did this and that: he fell on his face and also tore his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: A later חכם attacks רבי אלעזר's proof. He reads the פסוק differently, so יהושע and כלב did not only tear their clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר took the two פסוקים as describing two separate groups doing two separate things. The challenger points to the letter ו ("and") at the start of "וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ", which joins יהושע and כלב to what was just said about falling. So they fell on their faces too, and also tore their clothes. That weakens the idea that they were on a lower level.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (that the text reads this way)
He did this and that, meaning both

steps.confusionAlert: The challenger is not arguing about the wording of רבי אלעזר's rule. He is reading the פסוק differently: the extra ו means יהושע and כלב did both actions, not only the tearing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira challenged it,
and some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani:
If it had been written "Yehoshua",
it would be as you say;
now that it is written "And Yehoshua,"
phrases.notes: That extra letter ו means "and also". It ties יהושע to the falling that משה and אהרן just did.

phrases.english: he did this and that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof that רבי אלעזר brought in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's proof that יהושע and כלב only tore their clothes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ו in "וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ" joins them to the falling just described, so they did both actions. Nothing shows they were limited to tearing.

steps.title: Kings honor by standing, ministers by bowing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives another teaching: not everyone shows honor the same way. Kings show it by standing up, and שרים (ministers) by bowing. He starts the proof from a פסוק, which continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Not everyone shows honor by standing up, and not everyone by bowing. Kings show it by standing, and ministers by bowing. Kings by standing, as it is written: "So says ה׳, the Redeemer of ישראל, his Holy One…"
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new teaching built the same way as his last one. He starts quoting the פסוק that proves it, and the quote finishes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like tearing versus falling, here standing versus bowing depends on who the person is. Kings will stand, and ministers will bow. The proof about kings begins with a פסוק in ישעיהו. The rest of that פסוק, and the proof about ministers, come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing up as a sign of honor

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Not everyone [shows honor] by standing up,
and not everyone by bowing.
Kings by standing,
and ministers by bowing.
Kings by standing,
as it is written: "So says ה׳,
the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:7. The פסוק keeps going in the next part, where it mentions kings standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הַכֹּל בְּקִימָה וְלֹא הַכֹּל בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching of רבי אלעזר, built the same way as his "not everyone" teaching about tearing and falling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings show honor by standing, and ministers by bowing. The proof is still being given.
